title: UPC Coding
description: One coder's judgement that one code applies to one target (§12). A coding is deliberately a separate object from the extraction it labels: an extraction is the SPAN (content-addressed, so two coders selecting the same sentence converge on one id) and a coding is the JUDGEMENT about it (so two coders may agree, disagree, or multi-label without colliding). A coding MUST NOT carry its own locator — a span-level coding targets an extraction that has already passed the hop-B gate, which is what stops a code from becoming a back door for an unanchored span.

coding_id.description: cod-<12hex> (§06), content-addressed over codebook_ref + target.kind + target.id + coder + JCS({code}|{value}). What is OUT of that key matters as much as what is in: created_at, confidence, rationale, query and status are excluded, so re-running an unchanged coding pass is idempotent.

codebook_ref.description: The codebook this code is drawn from. Must resolve (dangling_codebook, §08).

code.description: A `code` token from the referenced codebook. Required for a closed codebook; forbidden for an open one.

value.description: Free-text label for an OPEN codebook (closed:false). This is model or human prose and, like extraction.text, MUST NOT be styled as a quotation (§09).

target.description: What is being coded. A coding never carries a locator of its own.

coder.description: STABLE handle for who made this judgement — e.g. "ra-column-v1", "ellie", "adjudicator". Deliberately not a model string: if the model version were embedded here, every model upgrade would re-mint every coding id and destroy agreement history. The volatile identity (model, version, prompt) lives in the coding-set manifest's coders[] and in provenance.produced_by. To compare two models as two raters, declare two handles — a deliberate act, not an accident.

status.description: Lifecycle, reusing §03's vocabulary. A changed answer on re-run mints a new coding and supersedes the old one rather than mutating a content-addressed id. Defaults to active.

codebook_revision.description: The codebook revision this judgement was made under. Advisory, and out of the identity recipe.

codebook_revision_digest.description: The codebook's revision_digest at coding time; a mismatch raises the advisory coding_codebook_drift (§08).

rationale.description: Why this code applies. Prose, never verified.

query.description: The question or task that prompted this coding pass.

ext.description: Tool-private extension data, namespaced by tool.
